Select the clips to validate

Source: R/select_clips.R
select_clips.Rd

Applies the sampling design to the predictions read by read_selection_tables() and returns the clip manifest: one row per clip to cut, with its site, species, night, source audio, start and end. No audio is read or written; cut the clips with cut_clips().

Usage

select_clips(
  detections,
  sampling_mode = c("top", "random_detections", "random_recordings"),
  occasion_unit = c("file", "minute"),
  threshold = NULL,
  n_top = 2,
  strata = "night_hour",
  covariates = NULL,
  recording_fraction = 0.01,
  n_recordings_per_site = NULL,
  recordings = NULL,
  audio_pattern = "\\.(wav|flac|mp3)$",
  recording_duration = NULL,
  min_confidence = 0.1,
  sites = NULL,
  date_start = NULL,
  date_end = NULL,
  species = NULL,
  hour_start = NULL,
  hour_end = NULL,
  alternate_days = FALSE,
  target_total = NULL,
  balance_by_hour = TRUE,
  max_per_species = NULL,
  remap_from = NULL,
  remap_to = NULL,
  seed = 2026
)

Arguments

detections

Predictions, as returned by read_selection_tables().

sampling_mode

"top", "random_detections" or "random_recordings". See Sampling modes.

occasion_unit

The occasion of the occupancy model: "file" (the whole recording) or "minute" (minute of the file, from file_offset).

threshold

Confidence threshold of the occupancy analysis. It defines the candidate occasions of "random_detections" and the n_detections_occasion column. NULL leaves that column NA.

n_top

"top": predictions kept per site x species x night x hour. "random_detections": occasions drawn per stratum (strata).

strata

"random_detections": the strata of the occasion draw (ignored by the other modes). Either one of the presets, all within site x species:

  • "night_hour": night x hour (the rule of 2.0.0);

  • "night": night;

  • "hour": hour of the day, pooling the nights (covers the diel cycle without fixing the night);

  • "week": ISO week of the night (YYYY-Www);

  • "month": month of the night (YYYY-MM), which spreads the draw over the season;

  • "site_species": no further stratification;

or a character vector of column names of detections, e.g. c("site", "species_code", "habitat", "night"), for strata defined by the user. Columns can be added to detections before the call; since site and species are always part of the strata, useful columns vary within a site (the moon phase, the rain of the night, a recorder when a site has several). month and week can also be used and are derived from the night when absent. site and species_code are always added to the strata, which keeps inclusion_prob exact when target_total or max_per_species draw again within site x species. Columns that depend on the score (confidence, rank) are refused, since the observation-confirmation design needs strata independent of the score, and every stratum column must be constant within an occasion.

With one recording per hour and occasion_unit = "file", "night_hour" holds a single occasion per stratum and draws nothing (every inclusion_prob is 1); a coarser stratum makes the draw random. With strata without the hour and balance_by_hour = TRUE under target_total or max_per_species, inclusion_prob is conditional on the first draw (a warning says so).

covariates

"random_detections": optional data frame of occasion covariates whose columns can be used in strata, such as the bins of an environmental gradient or of an acoustic index made by covariate_bins(). It is joined to the predictions by the columns it shares with them among site, night, recording_date, recording_hour, source_audio and occasion_id (compared as character; night and recording_date are YYYYMMDD). Occasions without a match form a stratum of their own, with a warning. A stratum other than site, species and time may be related to the verdict, so the calibration should include it or weight the clips by inclusion_prob (a message says so).

recording_fraction

"random_recordings": fraction of the recordings (or minutes) drawn at each site, rounded, with at least one per site. The default (1 %) suits large projects: with fewer than 150 recordings per site it draws a single recording; raise it or use n_recordings_per_site in small projects.

n_recordings_per_site

"random_recordings": fixed number of recordings (or minutes) per site, used instead of recording_fraction.

recordings

"random_recordings": the list of all recordings, as a data frame or the path to a CSV file with the columns site and source_audio (the v1.2.0 columns local and caminho_audio are also read). NULL lists the files matching audio_pattern in the audio folders that appear in begin_path; folders without any prediction are then left out.

audio_pattern

Regular expression for the audio files listed when recordings is NULL.

recording_duration

Length of the recordings (s), for occasion_unit = "minute" in "random_recordings" and for the end of whole-recording clips. NULL reads each file with the 'av' package when needed (minute occasions) and leaves clip_end as NA otherwise.

min_confidence

Minimum confidence of a candidate prediction in "top". NULL applies no filter. The random modes use threshold.

sites

Restrict to these sites. NULL keeps all.

date_start, date_end

Date window of the recordings ("YYYYMMDD"). NULL leaves that side open.

species

Restrict to these short species codes (the last part of species_code, e.g. "boa-ran"). NULL keeps all.

hour_start, hour_end

Hour window (0-23). It can cross midnight: hour_start = 17, hour_end = 2 keeps 17h-23h and 0h-2h, and the grouping becomes by night (small hours count as the night before). NULL applies no filter.

alternate_days

Keep alternate days (or nights), anchored on the first date of each site.

target_total

Total clips per site, split evenly among species by water filling: species with fewer clips than the quota enter whole and the surplus goes to the others. In "random_detections" it counts occasions. Ignored in "random_recordings". NULL sets no target. Because the target is split evenly, rare species have higher inclusion probabilities than common ones: estimates pooled across species must weight the clips by 1 / inclusion_prob.

balance_by_hour

Within each species, draw round-robin across the hours of the day (covers the diel cycle) when applying target_total or max_per_species.

max_per_species

Simpler alternative to target_total: a fixed limit per site x species. Ignored when target_total is set.

remap_from, remap_to

Replace the prefix remap_from of the begin_path paths by remap_to, e.g. "N:/" and "/Volumes/Arara/". Backslashes are turned into forward slashes first.

seed

Seed of every random draw. The global random number generator is left as it was.

Value

A tibble, the clip manifest without status, with the columns site, species_code, species_folder, recording_date, night, recording_hour, rank, confidence, clip_file, clip_start, clip_end, duration, source_audio, begin_path, sampling_mode, occasion_id, n_detections_occasion and inclusion_prob. See vignette("crywolf-integration") for their definitions.

Sampling modes

  • "top" keeps the n_top predictions with the highest confidence per site x species x night x hour. It serves classifier retraining and the score-to-probability calibration of calibrate(). Do not use it to estimate false-positive rates: top-score clips hold fewer false positives than a random sample.

  • "random_detections" draws, at random, n_top occasions per stratum (by default site x species x night x hour; see strata) among the occasions with at least one prediction of the species with confidence >= threshold, and keeps every prediction >= threshold of each drawn occasion. This is the observation-confirmation design of Chambert et al. (2015, doi:10.1890/14-1507.1 ).

  • "random_recordings" draws recordings (or minutes) among all those recorded, with or without predictions, in proportion to the effort of each site, for annotation by ear. This is the multiple-method design of Miller et al. (2011, doi:10.1890/10-1396.1 ). The clip is the whole recording (or minute), copied once per species to annotate, and confidence is NA.

In both random modes, use the same threshold as the occupancy analysis.
